India|is traditional knowledge patentabl.answer: Under Indian patent law, traditional knowledge is not patentable because an invention that is, in effect, traditional knowledge is not considered an invention [1], [3]. The law also excludes any creation that is an aggregation or duplication of known properties of traditionally known components [1]. Additionally, a patent can be opposed if the claimed invention is anticipated by knowledge, oral or otherwise, available within any local or indigenous community in India or elsewhere [5]. A patent can also be opposed or revoked if the subject of any claim is not patentable under the Act [4], [7]. Furthermore, the law places restrictions on sharing or transferring research results on traditional knowledge associated with Indian biological resources without approval from the National Biodiversity Authority [2]. Please note that this is general information and does not constitute legal advice.
